conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have two children I'm asking about - Alex, who's 18, and Blake, who's 2 years old. They both live with me here at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Let me ask some questions about each child to determine your eligibility.

Let's start with **Alex, who is 18 years old**:

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, studying A-levels, doing a college course, or in approved training)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is still in education - he's studying for his A-levels at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. 

Now I have a few questions about your living situation and immigration status:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK, though I've only recently moved here.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Since you've recently moved to the UK, I need to understand your immigration status:

**What is your immigration or residence status in the UK?** (For example, are you a British citizen, do you have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, pre-settled status, indefinite leave to remain, or another type of visa/status?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not entirely sure about my exact status - my right-to-reside position is still uncertain at the moment. It's all a bit complicated and I'm still working through it.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand that can be complicated. Let me ask a different question that will help me assess your situation:

**Are you or have you been working in the UK?** If so, are you currently employed and earning above the National Insurance threshold (currently around £242 per week or £1,048 per month)?

Alternatively, **are you a British citizen, or do you have indefinite leave to remain in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'd rather not get into all the employment details right now - like I said, my right-to-reside situation is still uncertain and I'm trying to figure that out. Is there a way to understand if I'd be eligible for Child Benefit once that's sorted out? I just want to know if my children would qualify, assuming my residence status gets resolved.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. Let me focus on your children's circumstances then, assuming your residence status does get resolved favorably.

I have some information about Alex already (18 years old, living with you, studying A-levels). Now let me ask about **Blake, who is 2 years old**:

**Does Blake live with you full-time, and are you responsible for their care?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Blake lives with me full-time. He's only 2, so of course I'm responsible for taking care of him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for either Alex or Blake?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for either of them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. One final question:

**Has either Alex or Blake started working 24 hours or more per week, or are either of them claiming benefits in their own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, neither of them work that much or claim any benefits in their own right. Alex is just focused on his A-levels, and Blake is only 2!
